open_questions: Lux and Minerals crafting costs ships: gems need ore (2 feed ships: cluster leg plus planet-to-station) plus silk, so at ship_cap 5 a full feed takes 3 of 5 ships and the lux run drops from a win (79-88 pct) to 41 pct. The bot keeps feeds to 2 ships (FEED_SHIPS), so lux never builds the Atelier (cask is not open without the tech) and min only crafts ingots. Is ship_cap 5 meant to make feeding that expensive?
Workshop output is 1 batch a cycle (3 armour = 540 base value), small next to a lane ship (about 560 a cycle). Do you want workshops to matter for share? Economy-designer call.
Seeds 1-3 are almost identical for focus runs (the sim has little randomness once chains are fixed). Should QA add noise or more chain/event variety?
handoff:
Bot-only changes in qa/bots/bot_run.gd; no game code or data touched. Tests pass=1165 fail=0. (1) _ranked_lanes now scores each lane with the real game numbers: engine.units_per_cycle(null, good) incl. skills, sold_price incl. skills, fixed_cost of that exact lane (route offset), lane must pass check_connection plus trade post; a lane whose one-shipment Buy exceeds cash is used only if nothing else exists. (2) Ships up to ship_cap: lanes with profit>0 qualify when cash >= 2 ships + upkeep or when already running, and the best lanes take a 2nd/3rd ship (lane_full rule), sync handles several ships per lane. (3) Workshops: built at ship_cap or with 2 ships of spare cash; feed cheapest planet source; ore fed via cluster->planet->station; own intermediates (cells) not bought; Sell in system 1 of a feed good is avoided (it drains the station). Crafting now runs in mil (armour+cells), bio (gel+seed), min (ingot). (4) --market=lux: bootstraps on any lane until the permit, then silk/musk lanes win. Focus runs learn their own tree first. Mining clusters in unopened systems are skipped.
